claim: DAVID syndrome results from NFKB2 heterozygous mutations, causing adrenocorticotropic hormone deficiency (ACTHD) and primary hypogammaglobulinemia.
source: Deficient Anterior pituitary with common Variable Immune Deficiency (DAVID) syndrome results from NFKB2 heterozygous mutations, causing adrenocorticotropic hormone deficiency (ACTHD) and primary hypogammaglobulinemia.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known association from prior research, supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: NFKB signaling plays a crucial role in the immune system.
source: While NFKB signaling plays a crucial role in the immune system, its connection to endocrine symptoms is unclear.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about NFKB signaling, referenced in the abstract.

claim: The connection between NFKB signaling and endocrine symptoms in DAVID syndrome is unclear.
source: While NFKB signaling plays a crucial role in the immune system, its connection to endocrine symptoms is unclear.
evidence: This represents a knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

claim: Introducing homozygous TBX19K146R/K146R missense pathogenic variant in hiPSC led to a strong reduction of corticotrophs number in pituitary organoids.
source: Introducing homozygous TBX19K146R/K146R missense pathogenic variant in hiPSC, an allele found in congenital isolated ACTHD, led to a strong reduction of corticotrophs number in pituitary organoids.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data presented in the manuscript, supported by qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence, and 3D imaging results.

claim: NFKB2D865G/D865G mutation acted at different levels of development with mutant organoids displaying changes in the expression of genes involved on pituitary progenitor generation (HESX1, PITX1, LHX3).
source: NFKB2D865G/D865G mutation acted at different levels of development with mutant organoids displaying changes in the expression of genes involved on pituitary progenitor generation (HESX1, PITX1, LHX3), hypothalamic secreted factors (BMP4, FGF8, FGF10), epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, lineage precursors development (TBX19, POU1F1) and corticotrophs terminal differentiation (PCSK1, POMC), and showed drastic reduction in the number of corticotrophs.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR and RNA-seq data showing differential gene expression in NFKB2 mutant organoids.

claim: NFKB2D865G/D865G mutation affected expression of hypothalamic secreted factors (BMP4, FGF8, FGF10).
source: NFKB2D865G/D865G mutation acted at different levels of development with mutant organoids displaying changes in the expression of genes involved on pituitary progenitor generation (HESX1, PITX1, LHX3), hypothalamic secreted factors (BMP4, FGF8, FGF10), epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, lineage precursors development (TBX19, POU1F1) and corticotrophs terminal differentiation (PCSK1, POMC), and showed drastic reduction in the number of corticotrophs.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq and qRT-PCR data showing changes in BMP4, FGF8, and FGF10 expression.

claim: NFKB2D865G/D865G mutation affected epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition.
source: NFKB2D865G/D865G mutation acted at different levels of development with mutant organoids displaying changes in the expression of genes involved on pituitary progenitor generation (HESX1, PITX1, LHX3), hypothalamic secreted factors (BMP4, FGF8, FGF10), epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, lineage precursors development (TBX19, POU1F1) and corticotrophs terminal differentiation (PCSK1, POMC), and showed drastic reduction in the number of corticotrophs.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing changes in EMT-related genes including CDH1, KRT8, CDH2, VIM, ZEB2, SNAI1, and SNAI2.

claim: NFKB2D865G/D865G mutation affected lineage precursors development (TBX19, POU1F1).
source: NFKB2D865G/D865G mutation acted at different levels of development with mutant organoids displaying changes in the expression of genes involved on pituitary progenitor generation (HESX1, PITX1, LHX3), hypothalamic secreted factors (BMP4, FGF8, FGF10), epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, lineage precursors development (TBX19, POU1F1) and corticotrophs terminal differentiation (PCSK1, POMC), and showed drastic reduction in the number of corticotrophs.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR and RNA-seq data showing altered expression of TBX19 and POU1F1 in mutant organoids.

claim: NFKB2D865G/D865G mutation affected corticotrophs terminal differentiation (PCSK1, POMC).
source: NFKB2D865G/D865G mutation acted at different levels of development with mutant organoids displaying changes in the expression of genes involved on pituitary progenitor generation (HESX1, PITX1, LHX3), hypothalamic secreted factors (BMP4, FGF8, FGF10), epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, lineage precursors development (TBX19, POU1F1) and corticotrophs terminal differentiation (PCSK1, POMC), and showed drastic reduction in the number of corticotrophs.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR and RNA-seq data showing decreased PCSK1 and POMC expression in mutant organoids.

claim: NFKB2D865G/D865G mutation showed drastic reduction in the number of corticotrophs.
source: NFKB2D865G/D865G mutation acted at different levels of development with mutant organoids displaying changes in the expression of genes involved on pituitary progenitor generation (HESX1, PITX1, LHX3), hypothalamic secreted factors (BMP4, FGF8, FGF10), epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, lineage precursors development (TBX19, POU1F1) and corticotrophs terminal differentiation (PCSK1, POMC), and showed drastic reduction in the number of corticotrophs.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence and 3D imaging data showing significantly fewer ACTH+ cells in NFKB2 mutant organoids.

claim: The results provide strong evidence for the direct role of NFKB2 mutations in the endocrine phenotype observed in patients.
source: Our results provide strong evidence for the direct role of NFKB2 mutations in the endocrine phenotype observed in patients leading to a new classification of a NFKB2 variant of previously unknown clinical significance as pathogenic in pituitary development.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data showing that NFKB2 mutations directly affect pituitary development in the absence of immune cells.

claim: The study leads to a new classification of a NFKB2 variant of previously unknown clinical significance as pathogenic in pituitary development.
source: Our results provide strong evidence for the direct role of NFKB2 mutations in the endocrine phenotype observed in patients leading to a new classification of a NFKB2 variant of previously unknown clinical significance as pathogenic in pituitary development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data demonstrating the pathogenic effect of NFKB2D865G mutation on pituitary development.

claim: ACTHD is defined by an insufficient production of ACTH by the pituitary, and then low adrenal cortisol production.
source: ACTHD is defined by an insufficient production of ACTH by the pituitary, and then low adrenal cortisol production.
evidence: This is a standard medical definition of ACTHD.

claim: Proper diagnosis and management of ACTHD is crucial as it is a life-threatening condition in the neonatal period characterized by hypoglycemia, cholestatic jaundice, and seizures.
source: Proper diagnosis and management of ACTHD is crucial as it is a life-threatening condition in the neonatal period characterized by hypoglycemia, cholestatic jaundice, and seizures (Couture et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Couture et al., 2012.

claim: Constitutional ACTHD can be isolated or associated with other pituitary hormones deficiencies.
source: Constitutional ACTHD, i.e., ACTHD diagnosed at birth or during the first years of life, can be isolated or associated with other pituitary hormones deficiencies, such as growth hormone (GH) or thyrotropin-stimulating hormone (TSH), then as part of combined pituitary hormone deficiency (CPHD).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about ACTHD presentation.

claim: ACTHD can be due to mutations in genes coding for transcription factors responsible for pituitary ontogenesis, especially TBX19, NFKB2, LHX3, LHX4, PROP1, HESX1, SOX2, SOX3, OTX2, and FGF8.
source: ACTHD can be due to mutations in genes coding for transcription factors responsible for pituitary ontogenesis, especially the T-box transcription factor TBX19 (also known as TPIT), NFKB2, LHX3, LHX4, PROP1, HESX1, SOX2, SOX3, OTX2, and FGF8.
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature about genetic causes of ACTHD.

claim: Mutations of TBX19 account for approximately two-thirds of neonatal-onset complete isolated ACTHD.
source: Mutations of TBX19 account for approximately two-thirds of neonatal-onset complete isolated ACTHD (Couture et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Couture et al., 2012.

claim: TBX19 is a T-box transcription factor restricted to pituitary pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)-expressing cells in mice and humans.
source: TBX19 is a T-box transcription factor restricted to pituitary pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)-expressing cells in mice and humans.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TBX19 expression pattern.

claim: TBX19 is essential for POMC gene transcription and terminal differentiation of POMC-expressing cells.
source: It is essential for POMC gene transcription and terminal differentiation of POMC-expressing cells (Lamolet et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lamolet et al., 2001.

claim: POMC is the precursor of ACTH.
source: POMC is the precursor of ACTH.
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge.

claim: Tbx19-deficient mice have only a few pituitary Pomc-expressing cells, with very low ACTH and undetectable corticosterone levels.
source: Tbx19-deficient mice have only a few pituitary Pomc-expressing cells, with very low ACTH and undetectable corticosterone levels (Pulichino et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pulichino et al., 2003.

claim: In humans with isolated ACTH deficiency, TBX19 mutations lead to loss-of-function by different mechanisms.
source: In humans with isolated ACTH deficiency, TBX19 mutations lead to loss-of-function by different mechanisms, such as the K146R (exon 2, c.437 A>G) pathogenic variant located in the T-box region, which results in a loss of DNA-binding ability (Couture et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Couture et al., 2012.

claim: The K146R TBX19 pathogenic variant results in a loss of DNA-binding ability.
source: In humans with isolated ACTH deficiency, TBX19 mutations lead to loss-of-function by different mechanisms, such as the K146R (exon 2, c.437 A>G) pathogenic variant located in the T-box region, which results in a loss of DNA-binding ability (Couture et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Couture et al., 2012.

claim: GENHYPOPIT is an international network aimed at identifying new genetic etiologies of combined pituitary hormone deficiency.
source: Thanks to GENHYPOPIT (Reynaud et al., 2006; Jullien et al., 2019; Jullien et al., 2021), an international network aimed at identifying new genetic etiologies of combined pituitary hormone deficiency, we described the first cases of DAVID syndrome, a rare association of hypopituitarism (mainly ACTHD) and immune deficiency (hypogammaglobulinemia) (Quentien et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Reynaud et al., 2006; Jullien et al., 2019; Jullien et al., 2021.

claim: The first cases of DAVID syndrome were described as a rare association of hypopituitarism (mainly ACTHD) and immune deficiency (hypogammaglobulinemia).
source: Thanks to GENHYPOPIT (Reynaud et al., 2006; Jullien et al., 2019; Jullien et al., 2021), an international network aimed at identifying new genetic etiologies of combined pituitary hormone deficiency, we described the first cases of DAVID syndrome, a rare association of hypopituitarism (mainly ACTHD) and immune deficiency (hypogammaglobulinemia) (Quentien et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Quentien et al., 2012.

claim: DAVID syndrome is associated with variants in the nuclear factor kappa-B subunit 2 (NFKB2) gene.
source: DAVID syndrome is associated with variants in the nuclear factor kappa-B subunit 2 (NFKB2) gene (Chen et al., 2013; Brue et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2013; Brue et al., 2014.

claim: A pathogenic, heterozygous D865G NFKB2 variant was found in a patient presenting with severe recurrent infections from 2 y of age, who at the age of 5 was diagnosed with ACTHD.
source: In particular, we reported that a pathogenic, heterozygous D865G (exon 23, c.2594 A>G) NFKB2 variant was found in a patient presenting with severe recurrent infections from 2 y of age, who at the age of 5 was diagnosed with ACTHD (Quentien et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Quentien et al., 2012.

claim: Mutations in the C-terminal region of NFKB2 lead to the disruption of both non-canonical and canonical pathways.
source: Mutations in the C-terminal region of NFKB2 lead to the disruption of both non-canonical and canonical pathways (Wirasinha et al., 2021; Kuehn et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wirasinha et al., 2021; Kuehn et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2014.

claim: Full-length NFKB2 (p100) protein has two critical serines, S866 and S870, in the C-terminal domain.
source: Full-length NFKB2 (p100) protein has two critical serines, S866 and S870, in the C-terminal domain.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NFKB2 protein structure.

claim: Phosphorylation of S866 and S870 sites yields the transcriptionally active NFKB2 (p52) through proteasomal processing of p100 protein.
source: Phosphorylation of these sites yields the transcriptionally active NFKB2 (p52) through proteasomal processing of p100 protein.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NFKB2 processing.

claim: The D865G mutation, located adjacent to the critical S866 phosphorylation site, protects mutant protein from proteasomal degradation, causes defective processing of p100 to p52, and results in reduced translocation of p52 to the nucleus.
source: The D865G mutation, located adjacent to the critical S866 phosphorylation site, protects mutant protein from proteasomal degradation, causes defective processing of p100 to p52, and results in reduced translocation of p52 to the nucleus (Chen et al., 2013; Kuehn et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2013; Kuehn et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2014.

claim: NFKB2+/D865G resulted in 50% of normal processing to p52, whereas NFKB2D865G/D865G exhibited near-absence of p52.
source: NFKB2+/D865G resulted in 50% of normal processing to p52, whereas NFKB2D865G/D865G exhibited near-absence of p52 (Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2014.

claim: The nuclear factor kappa B (NFKB) signaling pathway is a known key regulator of the immune system.
source: The nuclear factor kappa B (NFKB) signaling pathway is a known key regulator of the immune system (Lee et al., 2014; Lindsley et al., 2014; Carragher et al., 2004), which likely explains the immune phenotype of patients with DAVID syndrome, including susceptibility to infections and auto-immune disorders (Mac et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2014; Lindsley et al., 2014; Carragher et al., 2004.

claim: NFKB signaling likely explains the immune phenotype of patients with DAVID syndrome, including susceptibility to infections and auto-immune disorders.
source: The nuclear factor kappa B (NFKB) signaling pathway is a known key regulator of the immune system (Lee et al., 2014; Lindsley et al., 2014; Carragher et al., 2004), which likely explains the immune phenotype of patients with DAVID syndrome, including susceptibility to infections and auto-immune disorders (Mac et al., 2023).
evidence: This is an inference based on the known role of NFKB in immunity and the immune phenotype observed in DAVID patients, supported by citation to Mac et al., 2023.

claim: The underlying mechanism causing pituitary disorders in DAVID syndrome remains unknown.
source: In contrast, the underlying mechanism causing pituitary disorders remains unknown, with two predominating hypotheses: an indirect autoimmune hypophysitis, preferentially affecting corticotroph function, or a primary developmental defect suggested by the expression of NFKB2 in the developing human pituitary (Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This represents a knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

claim: Two predominating hypotheses for pituitary disorders in DAVID syndrome are: an indirect autoimmune hypophysitis, preferentially affecting corticotroph function, or a primary developmental defect.
source: In contrast, the underlying mechanism causing pituitary disorders remains unknown, with two predominating hypotheses: an indirect autoimmune hypophysitis, preferentially affecting corticotroph function, or a primary developmental defect suggested by the expression of NFKB2 in the developing human pituitary (Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: These are hypotheses from the literature, with the developmental hypothesis supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2020.

claim: NFKB2 is expressed in the developing human pituitary.
source: In contrast, the underlying mechanism causing pituitary disorders remains unknown, with two predominating hypotheses: an indirect autoimmune hypophysitis, preferentially affecting corticotroph function, or a primary developmental defect suggested by the expression of NFKB2 in the developing human pituitary (Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2020.

claim: A developmental role for NFKB2 was not confirmed in the mouse.
source: However, a developmental role for NFKB2 was not confirmed in the mouse: the Lym1 mouse model carrying a homozygous nonsense variant Y868* presented an apparently normal pituitary development and function (Brue et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Brue et al., 2014.

claim: The Lym1 mouse model carrying a homozygous nonsense variant Y868* presented an apparently normal pituitary development and function.
source: However, a developmental role for NFKB2 was not confirmed in the mouse: the Lym1 mouse model carrying a homozygous nonsense variant Y868* presented an apparently normal pituitary development and function (Brue et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Brue et al., 2014.

claim: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived organoids have emerged as promising models to study many developmental mechanisms and their perturbation in disease.
source: Over the last years, human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived organoids have emerged as promising models to study many developmental mechanisms and their perturbation in disease (Ho et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ho et al., 2018.

claim: 3D organoid models can replicate aspects of pituitary development.
source: Pioneering work on human embryonic stem cells and later, hiPSC, has established that 3D organoid models can replicate aspects of pituitary development (Ozone et al., 2016; Kasai et al., 2020; Matsumoto et al., 2019), and could thus be of major interest in modeling pituitary disorders (Ozone et al., 2016; Suga et al., 2011; Sasai et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ozone et al., 2016; Kasai et al., 2020; Matsumoto et al., 2019.

claim: Pituitary organoids could be of major interest in modeling pituitary disorders.
source: Pioneering work on human embryonic stem cells and later, hiPSC, has established that 3D organoid models can replicate aspects of pituitary development (Ozone et al., 2016; Kasai et al., 2020; Matsumoto et al., 2019), and could thus be of major interest in modeling pituitary disorders (Ozone et al., 2016; Suga et al., 2011; Sasai et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ozone et al., 2016; Suga et al., 2011; Sasai et al., 2012.

claim: The study applied recent progress in genome editing using CRISPR/Cas9 to a refined protocol to derive 3D organoids from hiPSC in order to model ACTHD.
source: In the present study, we applied recent progress in genome editing using CRISPR/Cas9 (Sun and Ding, 2017) to a refined protocol to derive 3D organoids from hiPSC in order to model ACTHD.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach of the study, with citation to Sun and Ding, 2017 for CRISPR/Cas9.

claim: The study validated the recapitulation of corticotroph cell differentiation in vitro by introducing a TBX19 mutation known to induce isolated human ACTHD and documenting the subsequent deficiencies in corticotroph development.
source: We validated the recapitulation of corticotroph cell differentiation in vitro by introducing a TBX19 mutation known to induce isolated human ACTHD and documenting the subsequent deficiencies in corticotroph development.
evidence: This is a summary of the validation experiments performed in the study.

claim: The organoid model displayed dramatically altered corticotroph differentiation in the absence of immune cells when used to characterize the D865G NFKB2 variant.
source: When our model was used to characterize the D865G NFKB2 variant found in patients with DAVID syndrome, it displayed dramatically altered corticotroph differentiation in the absence of immune cells, clearly demonstrating for the first time a direct role of NFKB2 in human pituitary development.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data.

claim: The study clearly demonstrates for the first time a direct role of NFKB2 in human pituitary development.
source: When our model was used to characterize the D865G NFKB2 variant found in patients with DAVID syndrome, it displayed dramatically altered corticotroph differentiation in the absence of immune cells, clearly demonstrating for the first time a direct role of NFKB2 in human pituitary development.
evidence: This is a major conclusion of the study based on the experimental data showing NFKB2 effects on pituitary development in the absence of immune cells.

claim: One KI clone carrying TBX19K146R/K146R was obtained after screening 100 clones by CAPS and confirmation by Sanger sequencing.
source: One KI clone carrying TBX19K146R/K146R was obtained after screening 100 clones by CAPS and confirmation by Sanger sequencing (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the experimental result of the CRISPR/Cas9 editing.

claim: In the 3D organoid culture method, pituitary-like and hypothalamus-like structures simultaneously develop.
source: The ability of the TBX19 KI line to differentiate into the hypothalamic-pituitary structure was compared to the control line (200 organoids for each line) using a 3D organoid culture method, in which pituitary-like and hypothalamus-like structures simultaneously develop (Figures 1E and 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data and figures showing both structures in organoids.

claim: hiPSC differentiates into hypothalamic progenitors in the central part of the organoids, whereas the outer layer differentiates into oral ectoderm, that will in turn develop into anterior pituitary tissue.
source: In this method, hiPSC differentiates into hypothalamic progenitors in the central part of the organoids, whereas the outer layer differentiates into oral ectoderm, that will in turn develop into anterior pituitary tissue (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data and figures showing the spatial organization of cell types in organoids.

claim: Organoids grew in the culture medium with average sizes in their greatest dimension from 0.4 mm on day 6–1.9 mm on day 105.
source: Organoids grew in the culture medium with average sizes in their greatest dimension from 0.4 mm on day 6–1.9 mm on day 105 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a measurement from the experimental data.

claim: In WT organoids, HESX1 peaked around day 6 of culture, and was rapidly downregulated from day 18.
source: In WT organoids, HESX1 peaked around day 6 of culture, and was rapidly downregulated from day 18 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is qRT-PCR data showing HESX1 expression kinetics.

claim: Expression of PITX1 increased from day 27, then reached a plateau from d48.
source: Expression of PITX1 (oral ectoderm marker) and LHX3 (pituitary progenitor marker) increased from day 27, then PITX1 reached a plateau from d48 (Figure 2E) whereas LHX3 peaked at d75 and was then slightly downregulated (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is qRT-PCR data showing PITX1 expression kinetics.

claim: LHX3 peaked at d75 and was then slightly downregulated.
source: Expression of PITX1 (oral ectoderm marker) and LHX3 (pituitary progenitor marker) increased from day 27, then PITX1 reached a plateau from d48 (Figure 2E) whereas LHX3 peaked at d75 and was then slightly downregulated (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is qRT-PCR data showing LHX3 expression kinetics.

claim: Immunofluorescence confirmed the presence of oral ectoderm cells expressing PITX1 and CDH1 (E-cadherin), resembling Rathke's pouch progenitors.
source: Immunofluorescence confirmed the presence of oral ectoderm cells expressing PITX1 and CDH1 (E-cadherin, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), therefore, resembling Rathke's pouch progenitors.
evidence: This is immunofluorescence data confirming the presence of specific cell types.

claim: The effective generation of pituitary progenitors was confirmed by the presence of LHX3 + cells in WT organoids on day 48.
source: The effective generation of pituitary progenitors was confirmed by the presence of LHX3 + cells in WT organoids on day 48 (Figure 3A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is immunofluorescence data confirming the presence of pituitary progenitors.

claim: LHX3+ cells were located in the outermost layer of WT organoids, surrounding the hypothalamic progenitor layer that expressed NKX2.1.
source: These cells were located in the outermost layer of WT organoids, surrounding the hypothalamic progenitor layer that expressed NKX2.1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is immunofluorescence data showing the spatial organization of cell types.

claim: By day 105, WT organoids contained many differentiated corticotrophs co-expressing TBX19 protein in the nucleus and ACTH in the cytoplasm.
source: By day 105, WT organoids contained many differentiated corticotrophs co-expressing TBX19 protein in the nucleus and ACTH in the cytoplasm, as seen in confocal microscopy, a critical feature for the rest of our investigations (n=8, Figure 3B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is immunofluorescence data showing differentiated corticotrophs.

claim: qRT-PCR results confirmed the highest levels of TBX19 and POMC expression after at least 75 d of culture in WT organoids.
source: Consistent with these images, qRT-PCR results confirmed the highest levels of TBX19 and POMC expression after at least 75 d of culture in WT organoids (Figure 2G–H).
evidence: This is qRT-PCR data showing TBX19 and POMC expression kinetics.

claim: Pituitary organoids in 3D culture mimic human pituitary ontogenesis.
source: Taken together, these data showed that pituitary organoids in 3D culture mimic human pituitary ontogenesis, and were characterized in our conditions by the ability to differentiate into pituitary progenitors by day 48 and into corticotroph cells by day 105.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined qRT-PCR and immunofluorescence data.

claim: Pituitary organoids were characterized by the ability to differentiate into pituitary progenitors by day 48 and into corticotroph cells by day 105.
source: Taken together, these data showed that pituitary organoids in 3D culture mimic human pituitary ontogenesis, and were characterized in our conditions by the ability to differentiate into pituitary progenitors by day 48 and into corticotroph cells by day 105.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings regarding the timing of differentiation.

claim: There was a significant decrease in the expression of HESX1 at d18 and d27 in TBX19 KI organoids.
source: Our data showed a significant decrease in the expression of HESX1 at d18 and d27 in the mutant (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is qRT-PCR data comparing WT and TBX19 KI organoids.

claim: Both PITX1 and LHX3 transcript levels were significantly decreased by day 48 and day 75 in TBX19 KI organoids.
source: Both PITX1 and LHX3 transcript levels were significantly decreased by day 48 and day 75 in mutant organoids (Figure 2E and F), with only partial recovery for PITX1 by d105, suggesting an impairment of pituitary progenitor generation.
evidence: This is qRT-PCR data comparing WT and TBX19 KI organoids.

claim: The decrease in PITX1 and LHX3 in TBX19 KI organoids suggests an impairment of pituitary progenitor generation.
source: Both PITX1 and LHX3 transcript levels were significantly decreased by day 48 and day 75 in mutant organoids (Figure 2E and F), with only partial recovery for PITX1 by d105, suggesting an impairment of pituitary progenitor generation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the qRT-PCR data.

claim: Although TBX19 transcript levels were unchanged until d75 in TBX19 KI organoids, a decrease in POMC expression was observed that was significant from day 48 onwards.
source: Although TBX19 transcript levels were unchanged until d75 (Figure 2G), we observed a decrease in POMC expression in the TBX19 KI organoids that was significant from day 48 onwards (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is qRT-PCR data comparing WT and TBX19 KI organoids.

claim: TBX19 expression was significantly higher in TBX19 KI organoids at d105, but this had no influence on POMC expression, which remained very low.
source: TBX19 expression was significantly higher in mutant organoids at d105, but this had no influence on POMC expression, which remained very low.
evidence: This is qRT-PCR data comparing WT and TBX19 KI organoids.

claim: The organoid model can recapitulate the need for a fully functional TBX19 protein to achieve proper POMC gene transcription during human pituitary development.
source: These results confirmed that our organoid model can recapitulate the need for a fully functional TBX19 protein to achieve proper POMC gene transcription during human pituitary development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the qRT-PCR data showing decreased POMC in TBX19 mutants.

claim: TBX19 KI organoid immunostaining on day 48 showed that LHX3 protein expression was decreased.
source: In line with qRT-PCR results, TBX19 KI organoid immunostaining on day 48 showed that LHX3 protein expression was decreased in TBX19 KI organoids (n=10 organoids for each group, Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is immunofluorescence data comparing WT and TBX19 KI organoids.

claim: By day 105, there were significantly fewer corticotroph cells expressing ACTH and TBX19 proteins in TBX19K146R/K146R organoids.
source: By day 105, we observed that there were significantly fewer corticotroph cells expressing ACTH and TBX19 proteins in TBX19K146R/K146R organoids (n=10 organoids for each group, Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is immunofluorescence data comparing WT and TBX19 KI organoids.

claim: 3D reconstruction confirmed that ACTH was nearly absent from TBX19 KI organoids on day 105 compared to control organoids.
source: 3D reconstruction confirmed that ACTH was nearly absent from TBX19 KI organoids on day 105 compared to control organoids (Figure 4A–B and Figure 4—video 1 and Figure 4—video 2).
evidence: This is light-sheet microscopy data of whole organoids.

claim: Corticotroph cell distribution was not uniform throughout the organoids, but was rather concentrated in one or a few buds.
source: We observed that corticotroph cell distribution was not uniform throughout the organoids, but was rather concentrated in one or a few buds.
evidence: This is an observation from the 3D imaging data.

claim: There was a significant decrease in the number of ACTH + corticotroph cells with a TBX19 KI genotype on day 105 versus control organoids.
source: In summary, there was a significant decrease in the number of ACTH + corticotroph cells with a TBX19 KI genotype on day 105 versus control organoids (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is quantitative data from 3D imaging of whole organoids.

claim: Genome editing of hiPSC with a KI homozygous pathogenic variant of TBX19 effectively prevented their differentiation into ACTH-producing corticotrophs.
source: Together, this first set of experiments demonstrated that genome editing of hiPSC with a KI homozygous pathogenic variant of TBX19 effectively prevented their differentiation into ACTH-producing corticotrophs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data on TBX19 KI organoids.

claim: Two homozygous KI clones carrying NFKB2D865G/D865G were obtained after screening by CAPS and confirmation by Sanger sequencing.
source: Two homozygous KI clones carrying NFKB2D865G/D865G were obtained after screening by CAPS and confirmation by Sanger sequencing (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental result of the CRISPR/Cas9 editing.

claim: There was no significant difference in the peak expression level of HESX1 between WT and NFKB2 KI organoids.
source: The results of qRT-PCR showed no significant difference in the peak expression level of HESX1.
evidence: This is qRT-PCR data comparing WT and NFKB2 KI organoids.

claim: Higher HESX1 expression in NFKB2 KI organoids from d27 to d75 suggested impaired downregulation of the gene.
